limitations: No data have been ingested or analysed by this project.
This source alone cannot attribute labour-market changes to AI.
Coverage, sampling uncertainty, revisions and subgroup availability must be reviewed before analysis.

title: Earlier signs of labour-market stress
summary: Test whether candidate indicators add useful warning time beyond ordinary labour-market baselines.
body: The research question is whether changes associated with AI adoption can help identify labour-market stress early enough to support economically vulnerable people. Association is not causation. A separate, credible measure of AI adoption or exposure is needed before evaluating the AI-specific hypothesis.
limitations: AI exposure data and a defensible identification strategy have not been selected.
A positive forecasting result would not by itself demonstrate that AI caused harm.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

details.Falsification: No improvement over the pre-specified baseline, or gains that disappear in held-out periods, would count against the forecasting hypothesis.

title: Change in unemployment rate
summary: A candidate measure of labour-market stress, defined in percentage points.
body: Proposed calculation: the unemployment rate in month t minus the rate in month t minus 12, using a consistent population, geography and adjustment basis. Record the rate definition and source vintage. This candidate is an outcome measure; its value as an early signal remains untested.
limitations: No values have been calculated.
Annual comparisons can mask recent turning points.
Seasonality, sampling error, composition effects and revisions may affect interpretation.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

details.Missingness: Return missing if either observation is missing
details.Threshold: Not set; must be calibrated and independently reviewed

title: Baseline and warning-time backtest
summary: A proposed test of predictive usefulness with strict separation of training and evaluation periods.
body: Pre-register the stress-event definition, forecast horizon and candidate predictors. Compare a simple historical baseline against candidate models using rolling time splits and only information available at each forecast date. Report warning time, false alarms, missed events, calibration and subgroup performance. Publish null and failed results with the same provenance as positive findings.
limitations: No experiment has been run and no performance metrics exist.
Predictors, target event, evaluation periods and minimum sample size remain to be specified.
Historical success may not transfer to future structural change.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

details.Reproduction requirements: Pinned data manifests, code commit, environment, parameters, seed and run log

title: Canada early-warning model
summary: A model specification under development, with no operational warning output.
body: A future model would translate validated evidence into an interpretable estimate of labour-market stress. It must document intended use, exclusions, input freshness, uncertainty, calibration and failure modes. A human review process must decide whether any signal merits action.
limitations: No model is trained or validated.
No alert levels, numerical thresholds or live signals are active.
Insufficient evidence is an unknown state, never an assurance of low risk.

title: Review readiness for earlier support

Potential options require a separate feasibility and equity assessment. This record does not authorize spending, eligibility decisions or intervention.
limitations: No implementing institution, budget or operational mandate is confirmed.
Effectiveness, distributional impacts and feasibility remain untested.
No individual-level targeting or automated decisions are supported.

title: Labour force characteristics of immigrants

body: Table 14-10-0471-01 is the primary public high-frequency source for the Canada pilot's immigrant labour-market stress outcome. It reports employment, unemployment, participation and related rates using three-month moving averages and is unadjusted for seasonality.
limitations: The three-month moving average smooths turning points and reduces apparent volatility.
The public table describes immigrant status but does not isolate refugees or asylum seekers; those groups must not be inferred from immigrant status.
Unadjusted seasonality, sampling uncertainty, revisions and subgroup sample sizes require explicit treatment.

title: Canadian employment trends in the era of generative AI
summary: Statistics Canada 2026 study applying complementarity-adjusted AI occupational exposure to Canadian employment and vacancy trends.
body: The study uses a complementarity-adjusted AI occupational exposure framework to group occupations into high-exposure/high-complementarity, high-exposure/low-complementarity and low-exposure categories. It reports that employment generally grew across these groups from November 2022 to December 2025 and did not find a clear persistent aggregate decline in high-exposure/low-complementarity jobs.
limitations: Potential exposure is not observed AI adoption, job displacement or causation.
The index relies on occupational-task information and expert assessments, including O*NET-based inputs adapted to Canadian occupations.
Aggregate patterns can conceal subgroup effects, including age, immigration status, education and job quality.

provenance.origin: Statistics Canada, Economic and Social Reports, January 2026
provenance.license: Statistics Canada Open Licence applies to Statistics Canada material; third-party index components retain their own rights.

details.Interpretive rule: Use as exposure evidence, not proof of AI-caused displacement

title: Use of generative AI tools among Canadian workers, March 2026
summary: Statistics Canada evidence on actual self-reported generative-AI use at work by occupation and AI-exposure group.
body: The March 2026 Labour Market Indicators release provides a direct adoption check alongside potential exposure. It reports substantially higher generative-AI use in high-exposure occupations than in low-exposure occupations and can help distinguish potential exposure from observed use.
limitations: This is a cross-sectional self-reported adoption measure, not a monthly historical series suitable by itself for backtesting.
Coverage excludes some populations, including the territories, people on reserves, institutional populations and regular Armed Forces members.
Use of generative AI does not establish whether effects are complementary, substitutive or harmful.

title: AI-exposed labour-demand cooling adds warning value for recent-immigrant stress
summary: Test whether deterioration in high-exposure/low-complementarity labour demand improves forecasts of recent-immigrant unemployment stress.
body: The forecasting hypothesis is deliberately narrower than a causal claim. It asks whether AI-exposure-linked labour-demand changes add out-of-sample predictive information beyond the recent immigrant unemployment series' own history. A positive result would justify further investigation, not the conclusion that AI caused the stress.
limitations: Recent immigrants are heterogeneous and may be concentrated in occupations with different AI exposure.
Aggregate time-series relationships risk ecological inference and omitted-variable bias.
Macroeconomic shocks, immigration-policy changes and population composition can move both predictors and outcomes.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

details.Null: Adding HELC labour-demand momentum does not improve held-out forecast error
details.Causal claim: Out of scope for this experiment

title: Recent-immigrant unemployment momentum
summary: Three-month change in the recent-immigrant unemployment rate used as the baseline stress predictor.
body: For month t, subtract the unemployment rate three months earlier from the current three-month-moving-average unemployment rate for the pre-specified recent-immigrant group. Positive values indicate deterioration.
limitations: The underlying series is already a three-month moving average, so this feature is intentionally smooth.
Seasonal patterns remain because the source is unadjusted.
Thresholds are not defined and should not be inferred from this feature alone.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

title: HELC employment cooling
summary: Negative three-month percentage change in employment for high-exposure/low-complementarity occupations.
body: When a defensible monthly HELC employment series is available, calculate minus 100 times the three-month percentage change. Positive values therefore represent employment cooling and align directionally with greater stress.
limitations: A defensible monthly HELC series has not yet been constructed from public data.
Occupation-level composition shifts can change the aggregate even without within-occupation displacement.
This is an exposure-linked signal, not a measure of AI use or causal displacement.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

title: HELC vacancy cooling
summary: Quarterly labour-demand change for high-exposure/low-complementarity occupations using detailed vacancy data.
body: Aggregate unit-group vacancies to the HELC exposure category using a fixed documented mapping, then calculate year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter changes. This is reserved for a quarterly robustness analysis rather than being mixed directly into the monthly primary model.
limitations: Quarterly frequency provides less lead-time resolution.
Vacancy estimates can be noisy at detailed occupation levels and may carry quality flags or suppression.
Vacancy declines can reflect hiring normalization or macroeconomic conditions unrelated to AI.

provenance.license: Project-authored record; reuse terms not yet assigned

details.Role: Robustness and corroboration, not the primary monthly predictor

title: Rolling-origin test of incremental warning value
summary: Executable backtest comparing recent-immigrant unemployment history alone with a model that also includes HELC employment cooling.
body: At each monthly forecast origin, train only on observations whose outcomes would already have been known at that date. Predict the change in recent-immigrant unemployment over the next three months. Compare a baseline model using recent unemployment momentum against an expanded model that adds HELC employment cooling. Report held-out RMSE and MAE and retain every forecast origin.
limitations: The experiment cannot run on real observations until the two input datasets are versioned and the HELC monthly mapping is resolved.
Forecast improvement would demonstrate incremental predictive association only, not AI causation.
Results may be sensitive to forecast horizon, training window, revisions and structural breaks.

provenance.license: Project-authored code and protocol; repository licence not yet assigned

details.Evaluation: Rolling-origin RMSE and MAE; no future-information leakage
details.Execution: Code implemented; real-data run pending versioned inputs

title: Relative HELC vacancy deterioration
summary: Difference between vacancy change in high-exposure/low-complementarity and low-exposure occupations.
body: The POC uses relative deterioration rather than raw vacancy decline to reduce false attribution. In the source-backed 2022Q4–2025Q3 comparison, HELC vacancies fell by about 50% and low-exposure vacancies also fell by about 50%, producing approximately zero percentage-point relative deterioration.
limitations: Approximate published values are used rather than a versioned raw extract.
Vacancy change alone does not establish AI causation.
Exposure groups are occupational aggregates and can conceal within-group variation.

limitations: The metric detects labour reallocation, not its cause.
Series were transcribed from a published Statistics Canada chart for POC validation.
Historical controls cannot eliminate every confounder.

limitations: No empirical Financial Runway distribution has been estimated.
Net worth cannot substitute for liquid financial resources.

title: Timely Transition Probability
summary: Scenario metric estimating the probability that a worker completes a transition within the effective transition window.
body: TVPM sensitivity tests calculate TTP as the share of simulated transition durations that fall within lead time plus protected runway. The mechanics passed monotonicity tests: more lead time or protection raises TTP, while slower transition assumptions reduce it.
limitations: The transition-time distribution is not empirically calibrated for sustainable transitions.
Scenario outputs are not estimates of programme effectiveness.
No operational TTP trigger threshold is approved.

provenance.origin: Canada POC v0.2 TVPM sensitivity test
provenance.license: Project-authored metric; source calibration uses public Statistics Canada data.

details.Definition: P(transition time ≤ effective lead time + protected runway)

title: Protected Transition Margin
summary: Candidate timing margin comparing available transition time with the time required for a sustainable transition.
body: PTM is retained as a candidate decision metric in the Canada architecture. The POC demonstrated coherent response to changes in lead time, protection duration and transition assumptions, but calibration remains too uncertain for operational triggering.
limitations: No validated sustainable-transition distribution exists.
Policy latency, eligibility and realized take-up affect the actual protected window.
No operational threshold has been frozen.

provenance.license: Project-authored metric.

title: OTPM-lite: exposure, deployment and labour-pressure gate
summary: Validated POC gate that keeps technical AI exposure, observed deployment and labour deterioration separate.
body: OTPM-lite asks whether high AI exposure is accompanied by observed use and differential labour deterioration. In the Canada validation, HELC worker GenAI use was high, but vacancy deterioration was not worse than low-exposure occupations and broad employment still grew. The POC therefore stayed in an active deployment/watch state rather than structural transition.
limitations: This is a proof-of-concept gate, not a production warning model.
Published summary values were used instead of a fully versioned ingestion pipeline.
Causal attribution remains insufficient and must stay separate.

provenance.license: Project-authored model architecture.

title: PEXM: population exposure heterogeneity
summary: Population exposure layer that preserves differences between migrant and non-permanent-resident groups instead of treating them as one category.
body: PEXM was validated on a top-10 occupational thin slice. Selected NPR groups have materially different occupational structures, so group identity must be retained. v0.2 downgraded the earlier directional exposure ranking because uncovered occupational shares create overlapping uncertainty bounds.
limitations: The thin slice does not cover full populations.
A complete population × occupation matrix is required for robust group-level exposure estimates.
Group identity is an analytical segmentation, not a vulnerability score.

provenance.license: Project-authored model architecture.

details.Core rule: Never collapse distinct NPR/migrant groups into one exposure estimate without evidence

title: VACM: vulnerability and financial-buffer layer
summary: Fragility layer that separates exposure to labour change from a household's capacity to absorb income loss.
body: VACM uses household financial resources and essential expenditure to represent shock-absorption capacity. The POC validated that recent immigrant families show different income-wealth distributions from established immigrant and Canadian-born families, while v0.2 established that true Financial Runway is source-feasible but still requires microdata engineering.
limitations: The POC did not estimate population-specific liquid financial runway.
Published aggregate wealth includes non-liquid assets.
Occupation, migration status and liquid financial data are not yet jointly observed in one public dataset.

provenance.license: Project-authored model architecture.

details.Recent immigrant lower-wealth share note: 45.9% across three income bands in pooled SFS table

title: PBGM: policy buffer and gap model
summary: Policy layer that encodes eligibility, timing, replacement and duration while exposing gaps between a shock and programme rules.
body: PBGM successfully represented EI, Work-Sharing and Worker Retention Grant parameters in the POC. The central unresolved issue is policy fit: a mechanism can look useful mathematically while statutory rules may not cover a deliberate efficiency-driven restructuring.
limitations: Rule encoding does not establish individual eligibility or take-up.
Programme rules can change and require dated source versions.
Work-Sharing shock fit for AI-enabled efficiency restructuring remains an open policy question.

provenance.license: Project-authored model architecture.

details.Core dimensions: Eligibility; latency; replacement; duration; realized take-up

title: TVPM: transition-window probability model
summary: Timing layer testing whether warning lead time and protected income support create enough time for a sustainable labour transition.
body: TVPM computes candidate timing metrics including Timely Transition Probability and Protected Transition Margin. v0.2 structural assertions passed: more lead time and more protected runway increase TTP, while slower transition assumptions reduce it. Calibration remains too sensitive for operational thresholds.
limitations: The transition distribution uses unemployment duration only as a provisional reference.
Sustainable transition requires origin-destination and pathway-specific evidence.
Credential recognition, training duration and job quality are not yet empirically calibrated.

provenance.license: Project-authored model architecture.

details.32-week window sensitivity: TTP approximately 83.5%, 71.4%, 59.2%, 38.7% as transition-time multiplier rises from 1.0 to 2.0

title: Canada Computational Proof of Concept v0.1
summary: Executed thin-slice test of the OTPM → PEXM → VACM → PBGM → TVPM computational chain.
body: The 25 September 2026 POC tested whether the modelling chain could run end-to-end using public Canadian evidence plus explicitly labelled scenario assumptions, without turning AI exposure directly into displacement or population identity directly into vulnerability.
limitations: Several inputs were manually transcribed from published summaries rather than ingested through a reproducible data pipeline.
PBGM/TVPM scenarios were illustrative, not population estimates.
v0.2 subsequently downgraded the thin-slice NPR ranking and revised the Financial Runway data-gap assessment.

provenance.license: Project-authored notebook using cited public sources.

details.Primary blockers: Liquid financial buffers; full population×occupation ingestion; pathway-specific transition time; policy eligibility/take-up integration

title: Canada POC v0.2 validation and data-engineering gate
summary: Executed validation of the Canada quantitative architecture using authoritative evidence, negative controls, coverage tests, sensitivity analysis and assertions.
body: v0.2 retained the five-layer architecture while tightening its claims. OTPM passed and the current structural displacement alarm was not triggered; PEXM heterogeneity passed while whole-population ranking was downgraded; Financial Runway became source-feasible but unestimated; PBGM rule encoding passed with an open shock-fit gap; TVPM mechanics passed while calibration remained unvalidated.
limitations: This is a proof-of-concept validation, not production calibration.
The original notebook has not yet been converted into a fully automated ingestion-and-run artifact in this repository.
Several source-backed inputs are summary values or chart transcriptions rather than raw versioned datasets.

provenance.license: Project-authored notebook using cited public sources.

details.Overall verdict: SHARE WITH CAVEATS - architecture retained, calibration not yet production-ready
details.Next step: Canada Quantitative Engine v1.0 - data ingestion + calibration

title: COVID negative-control occupational reallocation test
summary: Negative-control test showing that labour reallocation can accelerate without AI being the causal driver.
body: The v0.2 test compared occupational-mix dissimilarity in the AI period, COVID shock and a stable baseline. COVID reallocation was faster in the first months, while longer-window AI-period change was broadly similar to baseline change. The result validates the requirement for a separate AI-attribution layer.
limitations: Chart-derived values are approximate.
COVID is a useful but imperfect negative control.
The test demonstrates non-specificity of labour change, not the absence of all AI effects.

provenance.license: Derived research summary; Statistics Canada source under Open Licence.

details.Conclusion: Labour-change metrics alone cannot identify AI causality

title: Employment Insurance as reactive protection baseline
summary: Use EI regular benefits as the reactive comparator when assessing whether earlier mechanisms add transition time.
body: In the Canada POC, EI is not treated as anticipatory action. It is encoded as a post-layoff baseline so the project can compare how much additional transition time earlier retention or training mechanisms might create.
limitations: Eligibility varies by worker history and region.
Benefit caps and programme rules must be versioned.
This record does not imply that EI is sufficient for an AI-related labour transition.

provenance.license: Project-authored policy mapping using Government of Canada rules.

details.Role: Policy baseline comparator, not operational trigger

title: Work-Sharing as a candidate retention mechanism
summary: Assess whether Work-Sharing could preserve employment and create transition time before layoffs in a qualifying shock.
body: The POC treats Work-Sharing as an anticipatory-ish mechanism because reduced hours can preserve employment before layoffs. Its mathematical value is clear in transition-window scenarios, but an unresolved shock-fit gap exists for efficiency-driven staffing reductions.
limitations: Specific AI restructurings may not satisfy regular eligibility rules.
Employer and employee eligibility both matter.
Programme access, administrative timing and realized take-up are not yet modelled.

provenance.license: Project-authored policy mapping using Government of Canada rules.

title: Worker Retention Grant as a candidate retention-and-training mechanism
summary: Assess whether a Work-Sharing-linked grant could combine income protection with training to accelerate transition.
body: The POC maps the Worker Retention Grant as a candidate mechanism that can add training to a retention pathway. It is useful analytically because TVPM can represent both added protected time and a possible reduction in transition duration.
limitations: The mechanism depends on an approved and implemented Work-Sharing agreement.
Training effects on sustainable transition time are not empirically estimated.
The POC does not estimate take-up, coverage or effectiveness.
